examples.en: Rainfall is expected tonight.
There was little rainfall this year, so water is short.
The weather agency announced a regional rainfall forecast.
The baseball game was canceled because of rain.
A lot of rainfall was recorded in the mountains.
When the rain stops, the road will dry.

explain: '강우'는 비가 내리는 것을 날씨 뉴스에서 부르는 말이에요. 평소에는 그냥 '비'라고 하고, 비가 온 양은 '강우량'이라고 해요. 눈이 오는 것은 '강설', 비와 눈을 합쳐서는 '강수'라고 해요.
explain_en: 강우 is the word weather reports use for rain falling. In daily life people just say 비, and the amount of rain is 강우량. Snowfall is 강설, and rain and snow together are called 강수.

examples.en: A strong earthquake hit Japan and buildings shook.

examples.ko: 강진 뒤에는 여진이 이어질 수 있어요.
examples.en: Aftershocks can follow a strong earthquake.
Relief supplies arrived in the area hit by the strong earthquake.
Many people lost their homes in the strong earthquake.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 강진 소식을 계속 알려 줬어요.
examples.en: The news kept reporting about the strong earthquake.

examples.ko: 전문가는 강진에 대비해 건물을 튼튼하게 지어야 한다고 말했어요.
examples.en: The expert said buildings must be built strong to prepare for strong earthquakes.

explain: 강진은 규모가 큰 지진이에요. 더 큰 피해를 주는 지진은 '대지진'이라고 해요. 뉴스에서는 '규모 6의 강진'처럼 숫자와 같이 써요.
explain_en: 강진 is an earthquake of large magnitude. One causing even greater damage is a 대지진. In the news it is paired with a number, like 규모 6의 강진 (a magnitude 6 strong earthquake).

examples.en: In spring I sneeze because of pollen.
Pollen blew in the wind and piled up on the car.
Pollen can cause allergies.
Bees collect pollen and carry it home.
People sensitive to pollen wear masks.
The weather news reports the pollen level too.

explain: 봄에 '꽃가루 알레르기'나 '꽃가루 농도'처럼 건강과 날씨 이야기에서 같이 들어요. 한자어로는 '화분'이라고도 하는데, '화분'은 꽃을 심은 그릇도 가리켜서 헷갈릴 수 있어요.
explain_en: You hear it with health and weather topics in spring, like '꽃가루 알레르기' (pollen allergy) or '꽃가루 농도' (pollen count). The Sino-Korean word is '화분', but that also means a flowerpot, so it can be confusing.

en: water of a stream; water of a brook

examples.en: Children are splashing around in the clear stream.
It rained, so the stream swelled a lot.
Hearing the sound of a stream calms my mind.
In summer we play with our feet in the stream.
I walked up along the stream for a good while.
This stream doesn't dry up even in winter.

explain: '시냇물'이라고도 해요. 강보다 작고 졸졸 흐르는 물을 떠올리면 돼요. 비슷한 말로 '개울'이 있어요.
explain_en: It is also called '시냇물'. Think of a small, trickling flow of water, smaller than a river. A similar word is '개울'.

examples.en: A welcome rain finally fell after a long time.
The farmers waited for the welcome rain.
Thanks to the rain, the fields came back to life.
The rain that fell last night was really welcome.
The news reported rain coming tomorrow.
The trees turned green with the rain.

explain: 그냥 '비'가 아니라 오래 가물 때 내리는 반가운 비를 '단비'라고 해요. 비가 오면 불편한 사람도 많아서, 기다리던 비일 때만 이 말을 써요. '단'은 '달다'와 같은 뜻이라서 비가 달게 느껴진다는 느낌이에요.

phrases.example: 바쁠 때 친구가 도와줘서 가뭄에 단비 같았어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꼭 필요한 때에 받은 도움이나 좋은 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes help or good news that arrives exactly when it is badly needed.

explain_en: 단비 is the welcome rain that falls after a long dry spell. It is only used when people were waiting for the rain. The 단 is the same as in 달다 (sweet), so the rain feels sweet.

examples.en: A big earthquake happened in Japan.
A big earthquake comes suddenly, at any time.
That city went through a big earthquake long ago.
We prepare water and food for a big earthquake.
Many houses collapsed in the big earthquake.
A big earthquake is scary, but a tsunami is scarier.

explain: '지진' 앞에 '대'가 붙은 말이에요. 일상에서는 '큰 지진'이라고 풀어서 말하기도 해요. 뉴스에서는 '강진'이라는 말도 나와요.
explain_en: It is '지진' with '대' (big) in front. In daily talk people often just say '큰 지진'. The news also uses '강진' (strong quake).

examples.ko: 불이 나서 모두 건물 밖으로 대피했어요.
examples.en: A fire broke out, so everyone evacuated the building.

examples.ko: 태풍이 오기 전에 안전한 곳으로 대피하세요.
examples.en: Take shelter somewhere safe before the typhoon arrives.

examples.ko: 지진이 나면 책상 밑으로 먼저 대피해요.
examples.en: When an earthquake hits, we first take cover under a desk.
Residents are evacuating to the school gym.

examples.ko: 아이들은 선생님과 함께 천천히 대피할 거예요.
examples.en: The children will evacuate slowly with their teacher.

examples.ko: 홍수 때문에 대피한 사람들이 아직 집에 못 돌아갔어요.
examples.en: The people who evacuated because of the flood still can't go back home.

explain: '피하다'는 싫은 사람이나 일을 피할 때도 쓰지만, '대피하다'는 재난이나 위험 때문에 안전한 곳으로 몸을 옮길 때만 써요. 보통 '~(으)로 대피하다' 모양이고, 뉴스와 안내 방송에서 아주 자주 나와요.
explain_en: 피하다 can mean avoiding a person or a task, but 대피하다 is only for moving to a safe place because of a disaster or danger. It usually appears as '~(으)로 대피하다' and is very common in news and emergency announcements.

examples.en: Great floods often appear in old tales.
Last summer, the village was flooded by a great flood.

examples.ko: 대홍수 때문에 많은 사람이 집을 떠났어요.
examples.en: Many people left their homes because of the great flood.
I saw news about the great flood on TV.

examples.ko: 그 강은 대홍수를 몇 번 겪었어요.
examples.en: That river has been through great floods several times.

examples.ko: 대홍수 뒤에 복구 작업이 한참 이어졌어요.
examples.en: After the great flood, the recovery work went on for a long time.

explain: '홍수'보다 규모가 아주 큰 홍수예요. 뉴스, 옛이야기, 역사 이야기에서 자주 나와요. 평소 비가 많이 와서 길이 잠기는 정도는 그냥 '홍수'나 '침수'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a flood on a much larger scale than '홍수'. It often appears in news, old tales and history. When heavy rain just floods roads, people usually say plain '홍수' or '침수'.

examples.en: My umbrella flipped inside out because of the gust.
A sudden gust blew and my hat flew off.
The forecast said to watch out for gusts in the afternoon.
The child frightened by the gust started crying.
A rookie who appeared out of nowhere won the title.
The sign shook even in a light gust.

explain: 갑자기 세게 불다가 그치는 바람이에요. '태풍'은 열대 바다에서 생겨 큰 비와 함께 오는 큰 폭풍이고, '돌풍'은 짧고 갑작스러운 바람이에요. 뉴스에서는 사람이나 작품이 갑자기 큰 인기를 얻을 때도 '돌풍'을 써요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 큰 인기나 화제를 모은다는 뜻이에요. 드라마, 가수, 상품에 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means to suddenly gain great popularity or attention. It is used often for dramas, singers, and products.

explain_en: It is a wind that blows hard suddenly and then stops. A '태풍' is a big storm that forms over tropical seas and brings heavy rain, while a '돌풍' is a short, abrupt wind. In the news, '돌풍' is also used when a person or a work suddenly becomes hugely popular.

examples.en: When the whale breathed, a column of water shot up.
The fountain shot a tall column of water into the air.

examples.ko: 소방차 호스에서 물기둥처럼 물이 뿜어져 나왔어요.
examples.en: Water burst out of the fire truck's hose like a pillar.
A rainbow appeared between the columns of water.
The children played happily under the columns of water.
The column of water was as tall as a building.

explain: 굵고 높게 솟아오르는 물줄기를 말해요. 가늘게 흐르는 '물줄기'와 달리 고래, 분수, 부딪히는 파도처럼 힘 있게 솟는 모습에 어울려요.
explain_en: It describes a thick, tall jet of water rising up. Unlike the thin flowing '물줄기', it suits powerful scenes like whales, fountains and crashing waves.

examples.en: This neighborhood suffers flooding every rainy season.
There was flooding because of the rain yesterday.
The underground parking lot was a mess because of the flood.
School was closed because of the flooding.
Luckily, no one was hurt despite the flooding.
Volunteers gathered at the flood site.

explain: 큰비 때문에 생기는 홍수 피해뿐 아니라, 집 안에 수도관이 터져 물바다가 되는 일에도 써요. '물난리가 나다', '물난리를 겪다'처럼 말하고, '수해'보다 편한 말투예요.
explain_en: It covers flood damage from heavy rain, and also a home flooded by a burst pipe. It is said as '물난리가 나다' or '물난리를 겪다', and sounds more casual than '수해'.

en: force of flowing water; speed of flowing water

examples.en: It rained a lot, so the current got stronger.
Swimming against the current is really hard.

examples.ko: 이 강은 물살이 느려서 배 타기 좋아요.
examples.en: This river has a slow current, so it's good for boating.
The child almost got swept away by the current.

examples.ko: 다리 아래로 물살 소리가 시원하게 들려요.
examples.en: The sound of the rushing water under the bridge is refreshing.

examples.ko: 낚시꾼이 빠른 물살을 피해 자리를 잡았어요.
examples.en: The angler picked a spot away from the fast current.

explain: '물살'은 흐르는 물의 힘과 빠르기에 초점이 있어서 '물살이 세다', '빠르다', '느리다'로 말해요. 가만히 있는 물에는 쓰지 않아요. 바다에서 크게 일어나는 움직임은 '파도'라고 해요.
explain_en: '물살' focuses on the force and speed of moving water, so you say '물살이 세다/빠르다/느리다'. It is not used for still water. The big motions at sea are called '파도' (waves).

examples.en: At high tide the tidal flat is covered by water.
We have to go back before the tide comes in.
Today's high tide is around three in the afternoon.

examples.ko: 밀물과 썰물은 하루에 두 번씩 있어요.
examples.en: There are two high tides and two low tides a day.
The boat came into the harbor on the rising tide.
At rush hour people surged in like a tide.

explain: 반대말은 '썰물'이고, 둘이 같이 '밀물과 썰물'로 자주 나와요. 바닷물이 들어오는 때를 말해요. 사람이나 물건이 한꺼번에 몰려오는 모습을 '밀물처럼'이라고 비유하기도 해요.
explain_en: The opposite is '썰물', and the two often appear together as '밀물과 썰물'. It means the time when seawater flows in. You can also say '밀물처럼' figuratively for people or things pouring in all at once.

examples.en: Sunlight comes into the balcony well.
I dried the laundry in the warm sun.

examples.ko: 고양이가 볕 좋은 창가에 누워 있어요.
examples.en: The cat is lying on the sunny window sill.
Winter sun is short but really warm.

examples.ko: 이 방은 볕이 안 들어서 조금 어두워요.
examples.en: This room gets no sun, so it is a little dark.
My face got tanned in the hot sun.

explain: '햇빛'은 해에서 오는 빛이고, '볕'은 그 빛이 주는 따뜻한 기운에 더 가까워요. 그래서 '볕이 들다', '볕을 쬐다'처럼 짝이 되는 동사와 함께 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '햇볕'이라는 형태로 더 많이 들려요.
explain_en: 햇빛 is the light from the sun, while 볕 is closer to the warmth that light gives. It pairs with verbs such as 볕이 들다 and 볕을 쬐다. In daily speech you hear the form 햇볕 more often.

examples.ko: 올여름 불볕더위로 에어컨 없이는 못 살겠어요.
examples.en: With this summer's scorching heat, I cannot live without air conditioning.
The scorching heat has been going on for a week.

examples.ko: 불볕더위에는 낮에 밖에 오래 나가지 마세요.
examples.en: In scorching heat, do not stay outside for long during the day.

examples.ko: 이런 불볕더위 속에서 공사하시는 분들이 대단해요.
examples.en: The people who work on construction in this blazing heat are amazing.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 불볕더위 때문에 전기 사용량이 늘었다고 해요.
examples.en: The news says electricity use went up because of the scorching heat.
We went to a valley to escape the scorching heat.

explain: 햇볕이 쨍쨍 내리쬐는 심한 더위를 말해요. 습해서 후텁지근한 더위는 보통 '무더위'라고 해요. 뉴스에서는 '폭염'이라는 말도 같이 나와요.
explain_en: It describes severe heat from a blazing sun. Humid, sticky heat is usually called '무더위'. In the news you will also see the word '폭염'.

examples.en: The kids picked up fallen pinecones in the park.
A squirrel is gnawing on a pinecone.
I made Christmas decorations myself from pinecones.
Lots of pinecones have fallen on the ground.
Pinecones open up when the weather is dry.
I received a single pinecone as a gift.

explain: 여기서 '솔'은 소나무를 뜻해서 솔방울은 소나무의 열매예요. 청소나 칫솔처럼 쓰는 '솔(brush)'과는 소리만 같은 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: Here '솔' means a pine tree, so 솔방울 is the cone of a pine. It is a different word from '솔' meaning a brush, as in toothbrush or cleaning brush; they only sound the same.

examples.en: The whole roof was blown away by the typhoon.
He lost every bit of the money he had.
I pulled the tree out entirely, roots and all.
That person took my heart completely.
The thief took the whole safe.

examples.ko: 그 일 때문에 생각이 송두리째 바뀌었어요.
examples.en: Because of that event, my way of thinking changed completely.

explain: '통째로'는 나누지 않고 전부라는 중립적인 말이고, 송두리째는 뿌리째 뽑히거나 다 잃는 것처럼 하나도 남지 않는 느낌이 강해요. 그래서 잃다, 빼앗기다, 뽑다 같은 말과 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: '통째로' is neutral and means as a whole without dividing, while 송두리째 strongly suggests nothing is left, as when something is pulled out by the roots or lost entirely. It pairs well with verbs like 잃다, 빼앗기다 and 뽑다.

examples.en: I swept all the leaves in the yard away with a broom.
A huge flood swept away the small village.
I feel refreshed after sweeping away the dust.
The kids polished off the snacks in no time.
Let's sweep away all our worries and start fresh.
I sweep up the hair on the floor in one go.

explain: '쓸다'에 '-어 버리다'가 붙어 깨끗이 없애 버린다는 느낌이 강해요. 먼지뿐 아니라 홍수나 태풍이 휩쓸어 가는 것, 음식을 다 먹어 치우는 것에도 비유로 써요. 사람에게 쓰면 거친 말이 되니 조심하세요.
explain_en: It adds '-어 버리다' to '쓸다', giving a strong feeling of clearing something away completely. Beyond dust, it is used for floods or storms sweeping things off and, figuratively, for eating up food. Used about people, it becomes a rough expression.

en: low hill; hill near a village

examples.en: There is a low hill behind my house.
Every weekend I climb the hill and exercise.
I picked up chestnuts on the hill with my grandmother.
This village is surrounded by low hills.

examples.ko: 야산 아래에 작은 절이 하나 있어요.
examples.en: There is a small temple at the foot of the hill.
I heard the wildfire is spreading toward the hill.

explain: 높고 큰 산은 그냥 '산'이라고 하고, 마을 가까이에 있는 낮은 산은 '야산'이라고 해요. 산책하러 가는 동네 산을 떠올리면 돼요. '뒷산'은 집 뒤에 있다는 위치를 강조해서 불러요.
explain_en: A tall, big mountain is just 산, while a low mountain near a village is 야산. Picture the neighborhood hill you go to for a walk. 뒷산 stresses that the hill is located behind the house.

examples.en: We found an oasis in the desert.

examples.ko: 바쁜 도시에서 이 카페는 제게 오아시스예요.
examples.en: In this busy city, this cafe is an oasis for me.
Palm trees grow around the oasis.

examples.ko: 오늘 먹은 시원한 수박이 오아시스 같았어요.
examples.en: The cold watermelon I ate today felt like an oasis.

examples.ko: 그 도서관은 학생들에게 오아시스 같은 곳이에요.
examples.en: That library is like an oasis for students.
The camels drank water at the oasis.

explain: 사막에서 물이 있는 곳이지만, 한국어에서는 '바쁘고 힘든 곳 속의 쉼터'라는 비유로도 많이 써요. '도심 속 오아시스'처럼 광고나 기사에서 자주 나와요. '쉼터'는 앉아서 쉬는 실제 장소에 가깝고, 오아시스는 지친 마음을 살려 주는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: an oasis in the middle of the city
phrases.nuance_ko: 복잡한 도시 한가운데에서 조용히 쉴 수 있는 곳을 소개할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to introduce a quiet place to rest in the middle of a crowded city.

explain_en: It is the watered spot in a desert, but Korean also uses it widely as a metaphor for a refuge in a busy, tough place. It often appears in ads and articles as '도심 속 오아시스'. '쉼터' is closer to a real place to sit and rest, while 오아시스 carries a feeling of reviving a tired mind.

examples.ko: 어제 마당에 운석이 떨어졌다는 뉴스를 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw a news story that a meteorite fell in a yard yesterday.
I touched a real meteorite at the museum.

examples.ko: 운석 조각을 비싼 값에 사는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people buy meteorite pieces at high prices.
I gave a presentation about meteorites in science class.
I saw people looking for meteorites in the desert.

examples.ko: 떨어진 운석 때문에 지붕에 구멍이 났어요.
examples.en: The fallen meteorite made a hole in the roof.

explain: 하늘에서 불타며 떨어지는 빛은 '별똥별'(유성), 땅에 떨어져 남은 돌이 운석이에요. 일상에서는 '별똥별'을 더 자주 말하고, 운석은 뉴스나 과학 이야기에 나와요.
explain_en: The streak of light burning in the sky is a 별똥별 (shooting star), and the rock that lands on the ground is a 운석. In daily talk people say 별똥별 more often; 운석 appears in news and science topics.

examples.en: I hear a lunar eclipse will happen tonight.

examples.ko: 월식 때는 달이 붉게 보일 때가 있어요.
examples.en: During a lunar eclipse, the moon sometimes looks red.
I watched the lunar eclipse with my family.

examples.ko: 월식은 지구 그림자가 달을 가릴 때 생겨요.
examples.en: A lunar eclipse happens when Earth's shadow covers the moon.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 다음 월식 시간을 알려 줬어요.
examples.en: The news announced the time of the next lunar eclipse.

examples.ko: 월식과 일식의 차이를 과학 시간에 배웠어요.
examples.en: I learned the difference between lunar and solar eclipses in science class.

explain: 해가 가려지는 건 '일식'이에요. 달이 완전히 가려질 때는 '개기월식'이라고 해요. 뉴스에서는 '월식이 일어나다', '월식을 관측하다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: When the sun is covered it is 일식 (solar eclipse). A total lunar eclipse is 개기월식. News uses 월식이 일어나다 and 월식을 관측하다.

examples.ko: 이 지역에서는 겨울에도 키울 수 있는 작물을 많이 심어요.
examples.en: In this area, they plant a lot of crops that can be grown even in winter.

examples.ko: 올해는 비가 적어서 작물이 잘 자라지 않았어요.
examples.en: There was little rain this year, so the crops didn't grow well.

examples.ko: 아버지는 새로운 작물을 시험해 보려고 밭을 넓히셨어요.
examples.en: My father expanded the field to try out a new crop.

examples.ko: 태풍이 지나간 뒤에 작물 피해를 조사했어요.
examples.en: After the typhoon passed, they surveyed the crop damage.

examples.ko: 쌀 말고 다른 작물도 키워 보고 싶어요?
examples.en: Do you want to try growing crops other than rice?

examples.ko: 이 땅은 어떤 작물이든 잘 자라는 좋은 땅이에요.
examples.en: This is good land where any crop grows well.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '채소', '곡식'처럼 구체적으로 말하고, 작물은 농사 이야기나 뉴스에서 더 자주 나와요. 한 지역에서 키우는 식물을 통틀어 말할 때 편해요. '농작물'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: In daily talk people say 'chaeso' (vegetables) or 'gokshik' (grains) specifically; 작물 shows up more in farming talk and the news. It is handy for the plants grown in an area as a whole. You can also say 농작물.

examples.en: It rained, so the playground is muddy.
The ground was soggy and my shoes got soaked.

examples.ko: 비 온 뒤에는 길이 질어서 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: After rain the road is muddy, so be careful.
Rice that is too soft and wet doesn't taste good.

examples.ko: 반죽이 질게 되면 밀가루를 더 넣으세요.
examples.en: If the dough gets too wet, add more flour.

examples.ko: 오늘은 길이 질지 않아서 걷기 좋아요.
examples.en: The road isn't muddy today, so it's good for walking.

explain: '질다'는 땅이나 밥, 반죽에 물기가 너무 많을 때 써요. 반대는 '되다'(밥이 되다)예요. 'ㄹ' 받침 때문에 '진 길', '지니까'처럼 ㄹ이 빠져요. 사람에게 쓰는 말이 아니에요.
explain_en: '질다' describes ground, rice or dough that has too much moisture. The opposite is '되다' (as in rice being firm). Because the stem ends in ㄹ, the ㄹ drops: '진 길', '지니까'. It isn't used for people.

examples.en: A storm battered us all night.
The flight was cancelled because of the storm.
The ship ran into a storm and returned to port.
After the storm passed, the sky cleared.
It was a storm strong enough to shake the windows.
My umbrella flipped inside out in the storm.

explain: 세찬 바람과 비가 함께 오는 날씨예요. '태풍'은 여름과 가을에 오는 이름 붙은 큰 폭풍이고, '폭풍우'는 규모와 상관없이 비바람이 거센 상태를 가리켜요. 소설이나 뉴스에서 '폭풍우가 몰아치다'로 많이 써요.
explain_en: 폭풍우 is weather with strong wind and rain together. 태풍 is the named big storm of summer and autumn, while 폭풍우 describes any fierce wind-and-rain regardless of scale. You often see 폭풍우가 몰아치다 in novels and news.

en: to take refuge; to be evacuated; to flee

examples.en: Residents flee up the mountain.

examples.ko: 지진 때 우리 가족은 학교로 피난했어요.
examples.en: During the earthquake, my family took shelter at the school.

examples.ko: 태풍이 오면 높은 곳으로 피난할 거예요.
examples.en: If a typhoon comes, we will evacuate to higher ground.
The road was full of people fleeing.
A fire broke out, so we evacuated quickly and called.

examples.ko: 집이 물에 잠겨서 친척 집으로 피난해야 했어요.
examples.en: My house was flooded, so I had to take refuge at a relative's.

explain: 재난이나 전쟁에서 안전한 곳으로 가는 거예요. '대피하다'가 뉴스에서 더 자주 나오고, '피난하다'는 오래 떠나 있는 이야기에 어울려요. 몸만 피하는 '피하다'와는 달라서 장소로 옮겨 갈 때 써요.
explain_en: It means going to a safe place in a disaster or war. 대피하다 shows up more in the news, while 피난하다 suits stories of being away for longer. Unlike plain 피하다 (avoid), it implies moving to another location.
